cases.purpose: Five real pseudo-terminals owned by the side (devpts gid tty) with chosen modes and access times back synthetic USER_PROCESS records: -T/-w message status from the group-write bit (mode 0620 "+", 0600 "-", /dev/null and a missing pts/999 line), -u idle as "." (10 s), HH:MM (3725 s), "old" (90000 s), a future access time, and an access time older than a preceding BOOT_TIME record; -m with stdin redirected from a given terminal selects only its record, including with -T, -u, -H and -q. Regression also checks -w combined with -u and both orders of -q and -m, including non-terminal stdin; fixture setup failures are fatal.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils who 9.7 reading the same record files and stat-ing the same terminals
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr; each invocation is bracketed by markers on both streams and followed by its status. LC_ALL=C fixes the time format. -m runs in a subshell so the session-leader shell never acquires the terminal as its controlling tty. Terminal names come from the same allocation order on each side.

files.ptyhold.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Open pseudo-terminals, set each one's mode and access time, record their
# names and the time base, then hold them open until killed (takeover root).
import json, os, sys, time
now = int(time.time())
held, names = [], []
for mode, age in json.loads(sys.argv[2]):
    master, slave = os.openpty()
    name = os.ttyname(slave)
    os.chmod(name, mode)
    os.utime(name, (now - age, now - age))
    held.append((master, slave))
    names.append(name[5:])
with open(sys.argv[1] + '.tmp', 'w') as handle:
    json.dump({'now': now, 'ptys': names}, handle)
os.rename(sys.argv[1] + '.tmp', sys.argv[1])
time.sleep(55)
files.mkutmp.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Write glibc x86-64 struct utmp records (384 bytes each) from a JSON list
# (takeover root). Fields: type, pid, line, id, user, host, term, exit, sec.
import json, struct, sys
FMT = '<h2xi32s4s32s256shhiii4i20s'
assert struct.calcsize(FMT) == 384
out = bytearray()
for r in json.loads(sys.argv[2]):
    out += struct.pack(FMT, r['type'], r.get('pid', 0), r.get('line', '').encode(), r.get('id', '').encode(),
                       r.get('user', '').encode(), r.get('host', '').encode(), r.get('term', 0), r.get('exit', 0),
                       0, r['sec'], 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, b'')
with open(sys.argv[1], 'wb') as handle:
    handle.write(out)

cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
/usr/bin/python3 ptyhold.py pty.json '[[400, 10], [384, 3725], [400, -7200], [400, 90000], [400, 2000]]' </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
hold=$!
for ((i = 0; i < 250; i++)); do [[ -s pty.json ]] && break; read -r -t 0.02 _ <> <(:) 2>/dev/null; done
[[ -s pty.json ]] || { echo SETUP-FAILED-pty; builtin kill "$hold" 2>/dev/null; exit 97; }
mapfile -t L < <(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import json; [print(p) for p in json.load(open("pty.json"))["ptys"]]')
[[ ${#L[@]} == 5 ]] || { echo SETUP-FAILED-names; builtin kill "$hold" 2>/dev/null; exit 97; }
now=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("pty.json"))["now"])')
u() { printf '{"type":7,"pid":%s,"line":"%s","id":"%s","user":"%s","sec":1700000000},' "$@"; }
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py plain.utmp "[$(u 50 "${L[0]}" q0 u0)$(u 51 "${L[1]}" q1 u1)$(u 52 "${L[2]}" q2 u2)$(u 53 "${L[3]}" q3 u3)$(u 59 pts/999 q9 gone | /usr/bin/sed 's/,$//')]"
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py boot.utmp "[$(u 60 "${L[0]}" b0 before){\"type\":2,\"line\":\"~\",\"id\":\"~\",\"user\":\"reboot\",\"sec\":$((now - 1000))},$(u 61 "${L[4]}" b4 after)$(u 62 "${L[0]}" b0 fresh | /usr/bin/sed 's/,$//')]"
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py mesg.utmp "[$(u 70 "${L[0]}" m0 m0)$(u 71 "${L[1]}" m1 m1)$(u 72 null mn devnull)$(u 79 pts/999 m9 gone | /usr/bin/sed 's/,$//')]"
x() { echo "[$*]"; echo "[$*]" >&2; "$@"; echo "[status=$?]"; }
m() { local k=$1; shift; echo "[$* < tty$k]"; echo "[$* < tty$k]" >&2; ( "$@" < "/dev/${L[k]}" ); echo "[status=$?]"; }
x who -T mesg.utmp
x who -w mesg.utmp
x who -wu plain.utmp
x who -T plain.utmp
x who -u plain.utmp
x who -Tu plain.utmp
x who -a plain.utmp
x who -u boot.utmp
x who -aH boot.utmp
x who -m plain.utmp
m 1 who -m plain.utmp
m 2 who -mT plain.utmp
m 0 who -mu boot.utmp
m 3 who -q -m plain.utmp
m 3 who -m -q plain.utmp
x who -q -m plain.utmp </dev/null
m 0 who -mH plain.utmp
builtin kill "$hold"
wait "$hold" 2>/dev/null
